svg.text: GT Trackball - complete wiring (Pico 2 W, Bluetooth + USB)
Colour key: red = +5 V black = GND orange = 3V3 blue = trackball green = buttons purple = e-paper brown = control / sense. Pin numbers are the Pico's physical pins (1-40).
Top view (USB jack up). The Pico is mounted UPSIDE DOWN in the case, pins up: the GP labels printed
on the pin side of the board match this chart - wire by the printed labels, not by position.
outside: A-to-A cable to a PC USB 3 port
trimpot: set OUT to 5.00 V FIRST
also makes the battery sense ground common
low-side switch; gate R + 100k pull-down on board
Off until GP22 goes high; J1 holes come in groups of 3
(any hole in a group) - go by the labels on the back.
VSYS is boosted 5 V, so the cell is read here instead
GND screw to B- would bypass the charger's battery protection.
wire markings vary: go by position
- Bring-up order: (1) with NOTHING on VO+, set the charger/boost trimpot to 5.00 V. (2) MOSFET module on USB power. (3) battery sensor. (4) VO+ to VSYS + VIN+, pigtail.
- The charger/boost board replaces the separate MT3608 - it already boosts. Its only charge input is its USB-C jack, hence the short USB-C male pigtail from the Pico's VBUS/GND.
- Charging can draw up to ~1 A through the Pico's USB: use a USB 3 port (900 mA). If the port drops out while charging, the board's charge-current resistor can be raised.
- Sleep: GP22 low turns the MOSFET module off (trackball + ball RGB); GP7 goes low (button LEDs off) and a pressed button still pulls its GPIO low, so a press wakes it.
- The charger output is off (about 0.2 V) until its USB-C jack first sees USB power, then stays on (no auto-off).
- Never put 5 V on the e-paper VCC. All grounds are common. If the cursor moves the wrong way or the axes are swapped, fix it in config.py, not in the wiring.
